data: How We Became Modern: World History from 1750 to the Present

In this course we will study the history of the last two hundred and fifty years through a focus on key events that have shaped the modern world. This includes the end of European empires in the Americas and their growth in Asia and Africa, the emergence of nationalism, industrialisation and its environmental consequences, the world wars, the Cold War and globalisation. We will look at a wide variety of interesting historical actors from the gaucho cowboys of South America to the final remnants of the samurai in Japan. We will also encounter various important historical figures including Napoleon Bonaparte, Isambard Brunel, Joseph Stalin, Margaret Thatcher and Barack Obama. In studying this course we will gain a foundational understanding of the politics and history of the world in which we live.
